subject: Benchmark-backed capacity push for Q1 closes / Helios pilot sizing
messages:
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: sofiamarin@heliosai.com, procurement@heliosai.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Benchmark-backed capacity push for Q1 closes / Helios pilot sizing

Hi Sofia / Helios procurement team,

Great talking yesterday — per our conversation I ran the Helios sample workload through our internal benchmark harness. I attached the PDF with the token-level latency and throughput curves, plus a quick capacity estimate spreadsheet for the pilot volume you mentioned (~500k tokens/day, burst to 1.5M/day during onboarding).

Ask: to make your pilot SLA tight and avoid mid-quarter provisioning delays, can Redwood reserve a modest dedicated pool for Helios starting Jan 10 (Q1)? We want to pin a small tranche (8 x A100-equivalent slots) for the first 60 days and arrange burst credits if usage exceeds the baseline.

Why this matters: the benchmark shows that with the pinned tranche + prefix cache we can keep 95th percentile p99 latency < 180ms for your 1k prompt median. Without dedicated capacity we expect cold-start variability during spikes that would affect your customer demo.

Ben / Mina / Laura — looping you in to confirm feasibility on the ops and finance sides and to get a quick estimate of cost and slot availability. I’ve added the HubSpot deal link and the benchmark PDF.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben: confirm whether 8-slot reservation + burst credits is available Jan 10–Mar 10 and any constraints on SLOs
- Mina: short ops-runbook note for customer onboarding (KV cache warm-up, prefix pinning)
- Laura: preliminary cost estimate to present in the procurement packet

Sofia — if procurement needs a formal mutual action plan or PO template I can route our standard doc.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: helios_benchmark_v2.pdf (pdf), q1_capacity_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Benchmark-backed capacity push for Q1 closes / Helios pilot sizing

Jordan / team,

Thanks for the signal and the artifacts — nice work on the benchmark. Quick operational read:

- 8 A100-equivalent slots for Jan 10–Mar 10 looks feasible from pool standpoint today, but we need to lock by Dec 20 to guarantee the slice (hardware planning + node reservation).
- Burst credits: we can allocate a 2x burst buffer (i.e., additional ephemeral slots) behind a rate-limiter; requires approval from capacity team (I’ll ping infra ops).
- KV cache warm-up: I’ll draft the runbook; estimated 12–24h warm window when migrating models/weights. Recommend a 48h soft-warm period before external demos.

Constraints / risk: Q1 near-term churn on our fleet with a supplier firmware rollout in mid-Jan could impact availability on specific nodes — we can work around via node pinning but that increases cost ~6%. We should present that as a contingency in the procurement packet.

I’ll confirm slot hold feasibility by EOD Dec 15 and include a short ops note.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Ops Manager, Fleet Planning

Jordan / Ben —

Preliminary finance read below: based on the 8-slot reservation + expected traffic profile, earliest ballpark is:
- Reserved tranche (8 slots): $48k/mo (list), with a 10% discount for pilot commitments and a $6k/mo charge for prefix caching support/observability add-on.
- Burst credits: invoiced on usage; recommend capping at 200% of baseline to avoid runaway spend.

Ask from my side: can we produce a single-line cost table and an estimated monthly committed spend for inclusion in Helios’ procurement packet? Procurement will want both the committed-monthly number and the expected monthly with burst.

I’ll assemble the numbers into a small slide and share a draft by Dec 12. If Ben confirms any +6% contingency for node pinning, include that as an alternate scenario.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Jordan / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the benchmark doc. A few clarifications from Helios side:

- The 500k tokens/day baseline is conservative; marketing expects a phased ramp: Week 1–2 internal only, Week 3 external limited, Week 5 open beta. Peak bursts expected up to ~1.8M tokens/day for a 24–48 hour demo window.
- Procurement asks: can you provide a short PO template, and a one-page MAF listing the timing (Jan 10 start), payment terms (Net 45), and what happens if a supplier firmware event requires migration?

We’re aligned on the dedicated pool idea — locking by Dec 20 is acceptable. We’d like an initial invoice schedule for committed capacity and a sandbox billing account for burst usage tracking.

Sofia Marin
